es.text: Miau es una novela de Benito Pérez Galdós publicada en 1888 dentro de las Novelas españolas contemporáneas. Transcurre en el Madrid de la Restauración y es una sátira de la burocracia del Estado. Ramón Villaamil, un funcionario competente del Ministerio de Hacienda, ha quedado cesante por una serie de intrigas y lucha por recuperar su puesto mientras la familia apenas se sostiene. Con él viven su esposa, doña Pura, su cuñada Milagros y su hija Abelarda, a quienes la gente apoda «las Miau» por sus caras de gato, y su nieto Luisito, un niño enfermizo y visionario que conversa con Dios. Frente a Villaamil se alza su yerno, Víctor Cadalso, que prospera gracias a sus vicios. Con un tono tragicómico, la novela retrata la cesantía y la indiferencia de la administración hacia quienes dependen de ella.

en.text: Miau is a novel by Benito Pérez Galdós, published in 1888 as part of his series of contemporary Spanish novels. Set in Madrid during the Restoration, it is a satire of state bureaucracy. Ramón Villaamil, a capable official of the Ministry of Finance, has lost his post through a series of intrigues and struggles to win it back while his family barely gets by. He lives with his wife, doña Pura, her sister Milagros and his daughter Abelarda, whom people call “the Miaus” for their cat-like faces, and with his grandson Luisito, a frail, visionary boy who talks with God. Set against Villaamil is his son-in-law, Víctor Cadalso, who prospers through his vices. With a tragicomic tone, the novel portrays the plight of dismissed civil servants and the indifference of the administration towards those who depend on it.
